text: Change of approach, decided by the brain after measuring: cargo-nextest 0.9.148 ran the whole suite in 584 s against 673 s for cargo test on this 4-core machine (about 13% faster), not worth a new pinned tool and CI install step; do not adopt it. Instead make the slowest test binaries faster without removing or weakening any test: athena-cli tests/lifecycle.rs (174 s), tests/job_plan.rs (83 s), tests/drain.rs (61 s), tests/retry.rs (54 s), tests/steward.rs (48 s). Find where their time goes (for example real sleeps, poll intervals, deadlines, repeated repository setup, or serial locks) by timing them individually, and cut it: shorter test-only intervals, shared fixtures built once, avoiding needless real git or process work. Target: the full cargo test --locked under 6 minutes here. Record the before and after per-binary times (measured in the job) in docs/decisions.md, with the nextest measurement as a rejected alternative.
